body:
The 300ug trip manifested into a mystical mantra in my life, for Ive been consciously and unconsciously preparing for this trip for half a decade. Narratively, it was built up to be my lifes ultimate trip. I have experience in other psychedelics, including Shrooms, 2C-B, and Methallylescaline (Mescaline analog), but acid is my preferred psychedelic. This would be my 9th acid trip, and the psychonaut in me was ready to dive deep. The trip took place in my flat on a cool summers day. The big day was finally here.
I had a few intentions going into the trip: To peek behind the curtain. To experience ego dissolution.
I had a few intentions going into the trip: To peek behind the curtain. To experience ego dissolution.
To focus on continuity. In trip 2 (230ug), the CEVs freaked me out, but returning to that dose in trip 6 (250ug solo), I was ready. That trip gave me an introduction to ego dissolution and a taster of that fractal soup - I felt my atoms melting with the music. That experience was fleeting, and I wanted to go further and explore what that oneness and interconnection meant. I sensed there was something much grander, behind the curtain, where the ultimate truth might be uncovered on a higher dose.
On continuity, Ive often had an escapist attitude in life, whether through gaming or procrastination. I affirmed that the 300ug trip was not the end all and be all. Life will go on, with all the responsibilities that it entails. In fact, as I was cleaning my flat the night before, I left the drying rack with laundry in my living room as a reminder of the continuation of chores. I still have to go back to work on Monday, not to mention the deep integration to be implemented from the lessons of this trip.
I had a trusted friend trip sit me, and having been trip-sat by him and also having tripped with him before, I knew I was in good hands. Sober me set up a playlist, as I would not be coherent enough to select music during the peak. Pairing my favourite psychedelic tunes like Tame Impalas Let it Happen, Crumbs Locket with the classic albums, including Pink Floyds Dark Side of the Moon and Shpongles Nothing Lasts but Nothing Is Lost, I was so ready. At 12:56pm, I swallowed 2.5 gel tabs, dropped to the music video of A$AP Rockys Kids Turned Out Fine, emulating Rocky putting the tab on his tongue. Take-off.
It took 15 minutes to feel the first effects. As my mind ascended, the visual intensity accelerated. 45 minutes in, I knew I was in 300 territory, with visuals surpassing previous trips. Fractals enveloped my vision, and tracers became permanent. I was short-sighted, and at that point my vision became blurred, so it was better to just take off my glasses. My flat was turning cartoonish, but while shroom visuals resemble Legoland with defined edges, acid visuals are soft on the edges and rather circular. My kitchen turned into an illusion museum and my mind was still ascending. I had to sit down to pee, and the white walls in the toilet never felt so alive.
The peak was pure absurdism. Putting on my eye mask, I didnt just see. I felt. The I was dissolved and melted into the fractal soup. I peeked behind the curtain, and nothing couldve prepared me for what I saw. The universal consciousness appeared (at least, my subjective rendition) and felt simultaneous emotions of awe, fear, marvel, and disgust. There was cognitive dissonance. I have a primal fear of worms, and freaked out on my first ever psychedelic (shroom) trip. Because of that, I made a point of watching worm videos (Joe Rogan fear factor) and reading Wikipedia before every trip to acclimatise myself. The universal consciousness is a machinescape; an entanglement of pipelines, or perhaps worm-like structures in the sense that it was breathing, and all consciousness and energy could flow between them and was all connected. It was so visceral and haunting, yet, so natural and majestic. I knew this was a delusional construct of my mind, but it felt so real in the moment. This oneness is surely the common denominator for all high dose experiences, alas, it is just neurochemistry.
I went in and out of ego dissolution, with my trip sitters presence, that was a crucial reference point that enabled me to remain anchored to reality. At times, it felt as if I could enter the pipeline and enter his consciousness. But as my mind was being pulled into the pipeline, I felt a primal fear. I breathed and attempted to surrender and let go, but my ego was desperately clinging on. There would be no metaphorical death. Faced with the prospect of giving up everything that makes up who I was, deep down, subconsciously, I was not ready to let go. Thankfully Ive never had much suicidal thoughts in life, I suppose it might resemble the hesitation one feels before doing it. I think, to experience ego death implies a before moment just before crossing that event horizon. Luckily, I just had to take off my eye mask to abort the mission, but Im sure that a higher dose would be so much more treacherous for the psyche.
I was not ready to die. There, I rationalised that I had enough things going for me in life, and that meant that my life was worth living. I am a son, a brother, a friend, a colleague, a public figure in my professional field. There is too much to lose. I survived death by the thinnest of margins, here I was given a second chance. Hence, I must use this opportunity to live a good life. It was humbling and I was so grateful.
Time lost all meaning during the peak, and therefore I felt zero anxiety, for that is the fear of the future. There was only the eternal now, no past nor future. Deep down, I have an inner, true confidence, where I do not have to fake it in the moment, and it is a comforting reminder for times when my social anxiety is heightened.
There were two deeply introspective moments during the peak. I felt true empathy for my parents. I have always had an uneasy relationship with them, but it is not black or white. I left with a renewed understanding towards them. They truly meant well, but were held back by inter-generational trauma. I teared up as I understood this. We live in different countries, and I only get to see them once or twice a year. They get noticeably older every time I see them, and I am faced with their morality.
Playing Pumped Up Kicks, my favourite song, was cathartic. It was released when I was a teen, simultaneously representing nostalgia and longing, friendship and having a good time. I was so appreciative of my friends, my sitter, and how psychedelics allowed me to develop real trust. Earlier in the trip, my sitter showed me, for the first time, a private photo compilation of his favourite life moments, and I was in a few of them. To me, he was a private and reserved person, and to be shown this came as a pleasant surprise, which I really appreciated.
As the peak faded, my trip sitter was ready to depart. Going outside felt like spawning in real life GTA, with buildings, cars, roads, and sidewalk looking cartoonish. After parting ways, I walked around the neighborhood. The streets looked endless, patterns were found everywhere, especially on trees. Tracers were holographic, indeed, Tame Impalas Innerspeaker album cover was very accurate.
As I returned to my flat, the trip started to wear off, I attempted to make sense of what just happened. There was a contentious debate on ego death and what my close call meant. During the peak, my trip sitter confirmed that there was a level beyond this, where he has done 450ug a couple of times. I deduced that at that level, ego death was guaranteed, and there would be no negotiation. Whereas today, my ego still clung on, and I escaped relatively unscathed.
Up until now, I thought that my psychedelic journey would be completed at 300ug. But that was just the supervised phase. For me, if I make the leap to 450, then it should be a solo one, for that would be the psychonauts ultimate rite of passage. No trip sitter to anchor me to reality, just me, alone with my own thoughts, to really immerse, know myself, and let the drug do its thing. It is the ultimate contradiction - the ego chasing ego death.
Having consulted with ChatGPT about the 450 and ego death, I understand that a lot of research is required, including extensive engagement with the psychedelic literature. It was interesting to learn that so many different religions and cultures have their own conceptions of oneness and unity in relation to the self. It is simple to say next time I will know what to do. But it is truly not. Give psychedelics the respect it deserves, and you will be rewarded. I used to say I was ready to die, but how naive I was. Life is precious, and faced with the possibility of death, I was so, so scared to lose it all.
I managed to fall asleep by 6:30am without melatonin, and basked in the afterglow when I woke up around 12:30pm. That evening, I brought a housewarming gift and visited my trip sitters flat. He was a new homeowner and it reminded me of the treadmill of life and the real adult responsibilities we have today. The university days are over, and given the relentless demands and 24/7 nature of my career, there is simply not as much time that can be dedicated to psychedelics and drug experimentation.
Life is the real trip, but if, and when, I return to Lucy and pick up the phone again, I know exactly which ticket to buy.
